# Prologue {.unnumbered}

Welcome First-year Research Immersion (FRI) Peer Mentors! Thanks for
serving the next cohort of students as a mentor during the FRI Semester
1 (Research Methods: HARP 170) course at Binghamton University.

As a peer mentor, you will discover your purpose, adopt a unique
mentoring style to support mentees, and develop leadership skills to
support your research team. Great mentoring starts with
**self-awareness**: knowing your own mindsets, styles, and preferences
so you can adapt to your mentee and team. Each week follows a simple
three-step rhythm: a **brief** **mindset lecture or activity**, a
**self-assessment score and reflection**, and a **journal entry** that
turns the reflection into a concrete commitment.

::: callout-important
## Simulated data

Every score, table, and figure in this draft is **simulated** for layout
and review. Real results will replace them once the pre/post Qualtrics
survey is collected.
:::

## A Guide for You

This guide is your companion throughout the semester. Each week, you
will learn about a new mindset related to peer mentoring, review your
score on that mindset, and discuss how to answer the big question of the
week. Each chapter has the distribution for that week's measure and a
**password lookup table** where you can find your own score(s).

| Week | Mindset | Big Question |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | Mentoring Style | Does your style focus on structure or support? |
| 2 | Motivational Style | Is your motivational approach to promote or prevent for academics or social connection? |
| 3 | Leadership Focus | Is your leadership style to promote or prevent for the team? |
| 4 | Feedback Orientation | Is your feedback preference supportive or corrective? |
| 5 | Feedback Purpose | Is your feedback preference developmental or summative? |
| 6 | Leadership Role | Is your team's leadership positional or shared? |
| 7 | Leadership Target | Is your leadership style task or relational oriented? |
| 8 | Inclusive Mentoring | Is your mentoring inclusive? |
| 9 | Conflict Mediator | What is your conflict resolution style? |
| 10 | Goal Preference | What is your goal orientation? |
| 11 | Communicator | What is your communication style? |
| 12 | People Orientation | What is your view of people? |
| 13 | Self-Awareness | What is your self-awareness type? |

### How to find your scores

At the end of the anonymous survey you created a **password**. Each
chapter contains a table where you look up your password to find your
composite scores for that week's measure.

::: callout-note
## Save your password

Your password is the key to your individual scores all semester. Keep it
in your phone notes. To change it, contact the course instructor.
:::

### How to interpret your scores

Each measure produces a **composite score**, the average of your
responses to a set of related items (after adjusting any reverse-coded
items so all point the same way).

1.  **Find your score** in the password lookup table.
2.  **Locate it** on the class distribution. The dashed lines mark the
    **33rd and 67th percentiles**, and the shaded bands show the **Low /
    Mid / High** thirds of the class.
3.  **Compare** where you fall relative to your peers.
4.  **Reflect** using the two prompts at the end of each chapter.

::: callout-note
## There are no right or wrong scores

These measures capture orientations and styles, not ability. The purpose
is self-awareness.
:::
